parole.testo: From Andalusian Arabic البَرْغَات (al-barḡāt), plural of بَرْغَة (barḡa). Ultimately from the same source as abarca (“sandal”), probably Basque abarka.

parole.significato: the bush (remote, undeveloped area); the backcountry; the sticks; the middle of nowhere
parole.testo: Unknown. Proposed etymologies include: * From Andalusian Arabic [Term?]. * From Basque andur (“contemptible”). * From andar (“to walk”). First attested c. 1464-1474 (see quotations).
